messages:
Anya: quick heads-up — after enabling the FP8 path on the TP+PP config we saw a nasty perf regression on the 8xA100 cluster. p50 token throughput dropped from ~420 t/s to ~260 t/s and all-reduce time is dominating tail latency :grimacing:
Miguel: ugh. which config exactly? TP=4 PP=2? batch/seq?
Anya: yeah TP=4 PP=2, bs=8 (per-device), seq=2048, model ~ 20B. Torch 2.2 + our custom fp8 kernels. NCCL and nv driver current stable images. The odd bit: KV cache behavior looks OK most requests, but occasionally we see a KV re-sync (cache miss + full kv broadcast) which correlates with the long all-reduce spikes.
Perf-bot: auto-profile summary attached: flamegraph shows heavy time in ncclAllReduce during decode step for rank 0-3. CUDA kernels overlap poorly with NCCL ops. Top hotspots: ncclAllReduce (58% wall), fp8_quantize (12%), kv_merge (8%).
Kevin: interesting. my first thought — FP8 scaling mismatch across TP shards. if different shards pick different dynamic scales, then later cross-shard ops (all-reduce of accumulators or kv metadata) can cause inconsistent ranges, forcing syncs/fallbacks. those fallback paths would cause the re-sync.
Miguel: makes sense. do we quantize per-shard? we currently compute scale = max(abs(x)).to(device_shard) and then quantize. we do an all-reduce of the quantized tensors but not of the scales.
Anya: right now scale is local. I'll repro with sharing the scale before quantization.
Kevin: also look at communication/compute overlap. we might be launching NCCL on the default stream and blocking compute. try moving NCCL ops to a dedicated comm stream and use CUDA events to overlap. pseudocode:
```
comm_stream = torch.cuda.Stream(device=dev)
with torch.cuda.stream(comm_stream):
    nccl_allreduce(tensor)
# mark event
event.record(comm_stream)
# wait in compute stream
compute_stream.wait_event(event)
```
Miguel: good call. we should also check fusion thresholds — tiny tensors lead to many small all-reduces. tensor fusion (grouping buffers) would amortize startup. our current fusion threshold is 256KB, maybe too low for seq=2k decoding slices.
Anya: ran two quick experiments this morning: 1) share-per-shard-scale (all-reduce max) before quantize -> cut the rare re-syncs but p50 only improved to ~310 t/s. 2) move NCCL to comm stream + tensor fusion increase (to 1MB) -> p50 ~380 t/s, all-reduce share down to ~28% of wall. combined gave ~390 t/s. still not baseline but much closer.
Sue: numbers look promising. did you profile NVLink vs PCIe paths? multi-GPU topology changes cause different P2P levels and can blow up latency.
Anya: good point — we run mixed host topologies in the cluster. I tested on single-rack NVLink mesh and got the 390 t/s; on cross-rack (IB) it was still ~250 t/s with occasional nccl protocol fallbacks.
Kevin: for cross-rack, consider hierarchical all-reduce: reduce within node first, then ring across nodes. NCCL sometimes picks suboptimal proto when tensors are FP8/INT8 (small packed buffers). forcing protocol or using `ncclComm` topology hints can help. also try enabling NCCL fuse (tensor aggregation) at the framework level.
Miguel: another angle — reduce precision accumulation. if we all-reduce on fp8/uint8 payloads, accumulation rounding can create numerical drift and codepaths might do extra checks (we have sanity asserts in debug builds). confirm we don't trigger debug assertions in prod.
Anya: confirmed: debug asserts disabled. but numerical drift shows up as tiny diffs in KV keys (float crop) which then fail exact-match caches -> cache miss -> full broadcast. so we need canonicalization: deterministic quantization or a small deterministic hash over float values instead of relying on exact equality.
Kevin: or keep KV keys in FP32, only quantize token logits/activations. that reduces traffic for KV index all-reduces. tradeoff: more memory, less comm/precision flakiness.
Perf-bot: quick raw numbers from today's jobs (single-rack NVLink): baseline FP32=422 t/s, naive FP8(no-scale-share)=263 t/s, FP8+scale-share=310 t/s, FP8+comm-stream+1MB-fusion=389 t/s. cross-rack IB: baseline ~410 t/s, FP8 combined ~250 t/s.
Miguel: sounds like action items: (1) make scale-sharing default for TP quant path, (2) move NCCL launches to comm stream + add fusion buffer grouping, (3) change KV indexing to canonical (FP32 keys or deterministic hash), (4) add an infra test that runs TP+PP with FP8 on cross-rack variant.
Anya: will do. I'll open a PR with the scale-share patch and perf harness. assigning @Kevin and @Miguel to help validate hierarchical all-reduce options and comm-stream templates. I'll drop nsight traces in the ticket.
Kevin: for the nsight capture, recommended command:
```
nsys profile -o trace_tp_fp8 --trace=cuda,nccl python -u tools/decode_bench.py --model ...
# or: nvprof --profile-from-start off --csv --log-file nvprof.csv python ...
```
Miguel: also enable envs while testing: `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0` and try `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL`/`SYS` variants depending on topology.
Anya: noted. I'll run the cross-rack microbench today and post traces. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Ops-Bot: @channel New perf ticket created: INF-9843 "tp fp8 comm/compute overlap + kv canonicalization" — assignees: Anya, Kevin, Miguel. ETA 2w.
Anya: added the initial flamegraphs and a short repro script to the ticket. ping if you need access to the isolated rack.
Kevin: if we get the hierarchical all-reduce + deterministic kv keys in place, I think we can safely turn FP8 on for dedicated clusters. still need to watch edge-case rescaling when activations saturate.
Miguel: I'll prototype a per-step global-scale-aggregation (max across shards) approach so dynamic range is consistent even with transient spikes.
Anya: great. will keep thread updated with numbers. thanks :eyes:
